units.section_text:
3.3 NERC CIP Activities Permitted for Delegation 
Pursuant to the NERC CIP Standards certain activities required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager may 
not be delegated. These are activities that the NERC CIP Standards have defined as obligations 
specifically required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager.  
Ownership and accountability for NERC CIP activities that are not CIP Senior Manager obligations are 
managed through other compliance procedures and do not need to be delegated in accordance with 
this Process.  
The following are NERC CIP Standards activities that have been approved by the COO and relevant 
senior leadership for delegation by the CIP Senior Manager:  
CIP Senior Manager Delegations 
3.3.1 
CIP-002-5.1a, R2.2: Approve the identifications of the high, medium, and low BES Cyber 
Systems required by Requirement R1 at least once every 15 calendar months, even if it has no 
identified items in Requirement R1. 
3.3.2 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), R4: The Responsible Entity may delegate authority 
for specific actions under one or more cyber security policies to a delegate or delegates where 
allowed by the NERC CIP Standards. These delegations shall be documented in accordance 
with Section 3.2 and updated within 30 days of any change to the delegation.  
3.3.3 
CIP-007-6, R2.4: For each mitigation plan created or revised in R2.4, Part 2.3, implement the 
plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to 
the timeframe specified in Part 2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate. 
3.3.4 
CIP-013-2, R3: Each Responsible Entity shall review and obtain CIP Senior Manager or delegate 
approval of its supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) specified in Requirement 
R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Delegations 
3.3.5 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), Attachment 1, Section 5: Each Responsible Entity 
shall, except under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, implement plans to achieve the objective 
of mitigating risk of the introduction of malicious code to low impact BES Cyber Systems 
through the use of Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media. 

[LSP CIP Senior Manager Process] | Page 7 of 10 
Private – For Internal Use Only 
3.3.6 
CIP-004-7, R2.2: Require completion of the training specified in R2.2, Part 2.1 prior to granting 
authorized electronic access and authorized unescorted physical access to applicable Cyber 
Assets, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. 
3.3.7 
CIP-004-7, R4.1-R4.1.3: Process to authorize based on need, as determined by the 
Responsible Entity, except for CIP Exceptional Circumstances: electronic access; unescorted 
physical access into a Physical Security Perimeter; and access to designated storage locations, 
whether physical or electronic, for BES Cyber System Information. 
3.3.8 
CIP-006-6, R2.1 and R2.2: Require continuous escorted access of visitors (individuals who are 
provided access but are not authorized for unescorted physical access) within each Physical 
Security Perimeter, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. Require manual or 
automated logging of visitor entry into and exit from the Physical Security Perimeter that 
includes date and time of the initial entry and last exit, the visitor’s name, and the name of an 
individual point of contact responsible for the visitor, except during CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.9 
CIP-007-6, R4.3: Where technically feasible, retain applicable event logs identified in R4.3, Part 
4.1 for at least the last 90 consecutive calendar days except under CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.10 CIP-010-4, R3.3: Prior to adding a new applicable Cyber Asset to a production environment, 
perform an active vulnerability assessment of the new Cyber Asset, except for CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances and like replacements of the same type of Cyber Asset with a baseline 
configuration that models an existing baseline configuration of the previous or other existing 
Cyber Asset. 
3.3.11 
CIP-010-4, R4: Each Responsible Entity, for its high impact and medium impact BES Cyber 
Systems and associated Protected Cyber Assets, shall implement, except under CIP 
Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) for Transient Cyber Assets and 
Removable Media that include the sections in Attachment 1. 
3.3.12 
CIP-012-1 (CIP-012-2, effective 7/1/26), R1: The Responsible Entity shall implement, except 
under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) to mitigate the risks 
posed by unauthorized disclosure and unauthorized modification of Real-time Assessment and 
Real-time monitoring data while being transmitted between any applicable Control Centers.

units.section_text:
3.1 
Designation of CIP Senior Manager 
To ensure our commitment to compliance with the NERC CIP Standards’ obligations, LS Power has 
assigned a single CIP Senior Manager with overall responsibility and authority for leading and managing 
the Company’s implementation and adherence to the NERC CIP Standards. 
The designated NERC CIP Senior Manager may delegate certain responsibilities as permitted by the 
NERC CIP Standards. In addition to setting forth the CIP Senior Manager Designation commitment, this 
Process provides the procedures to be followed for CIP Senior Manager related designation and 
delegation responsibilities to ensure continued compliance.  
3.1.1 
The NERC CIP Senior Manager is designated by LS Power’s Chief Operating Officer (COO) in 
coordination with business unit and other relevant senior leadership. The official designation of 
the CIP Senior Manager is documented in accordance with Appendix A of this process, LS 
Power NERC CIP Senior Manager Designation. 
3.1.2 
The CIP Senior Manager must approve LS Power Cyber Security Policies for high impact, 
medium impact and assets containing low BES Cyber Systems in accordance with CIP-003-8 
(CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. This approval may not 
be delegated however the CIP Senior Manager may delegate other responsibilities as described 
within this policy. Refer to Section 3.2 below and CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26) 
Cyber Security Policies. 
3.1.3 
Any changes to the CIP Senior Manager shall be documented within 30 calendar days of the 
effective date of the change. (Refer to Appendix A for designation form).

3.1.3 
Personnel Risk Assessment Program (R3) 
3.1.3.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a personnel risk assessment program for personnel who 
require authorized electronic or authorized unescorted physical access to BES Cyber 
Systems. The personnel risk assessment program shall include the following elements: 
• 
Process to confirm identity (Part 3.1), 
• 
Process to perform a seven-year criminal history records check including current 
residence, regardless of duration and other locations where, during the seven years 
immediately prior to the date of the criminal history records check, the subject has 
resided for six consecutive months or more (Part 3.2, Part 3.2.1, Part 3.2.2), 
• 
Process to evaluate criminal history checks for authorizing access (Part 3.3), 
• 
Process to verify vendor, contractor, and consultants meet requirements (Part 3.1, Part 
3.3, Part 3.4), and 
• 
Process to ensure individuals with authorized unescorted physical access and/or 
authorized electronic access complete a personnel risk assessment at least every seven 
years (Part 3.5).

units.section_text:
3.1.4 Access Management Program (R4) 
3.1.4.1 
LSPG shall document and implement an access management program based upon need, for 
authorizing electronic access, unescorted physical access into a Physical Security Perimeter 
(PSP), and electronic and/or physical access to BES Cyber System Information (BCSI), except 
for CIP Exceptional Circumstances (Part 4.1, Part 4.1.1, Part 4.1.2, and Part 4.1.3). 
3.1.4.2 
LSPG shall require, at least each calendar quarter, verification of authorization and 
documentation for individuals with active electronic access or unescorted physical access 
(Part 4.2). 
3.1.4.3 
LSPG shall require, at least once every 15 calendar months, verification that all user accounts, 
user account groups, or user role categories, and their specific associated privileges are 
correct and are necessary (Part 4.3). 
3.1.4.4 
Prior to provisioning, LSPG shall require authorization (unless already authorized according to 
4.1) based on need, as determined by the responsible entity, except for CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances; Provisioned electronic access to electronic BCSI and provisioned physical 
access to physical BCSI (6.1.1 & 6.1.2) 
3.1.4.5 
LSPG shall require, at least once every 15 calendar months, verification that all provisioned 
access to BSCI is authorized and appropriate based on need as determined by the 
responsible entity (Part 6.2.1 and 6.2.2).

units.section_text:
3.1 Requesting Physical Access, Electronic Access, and/or Access to Electronic Storage 
Locations including BCSI Repositories 
Note: A completed Personnel Risk Assessment (PRA) and NERC CIP training is required to be 
completed prior to granting unescorted physical access, electronic access, or access to BCSI. Refer 
to OT Personnel Risk Assessment Procedure for instructions on the PRA process and OT Cyber 
Security Training and Awareness Procedure for instructions on completing the NERC CIP training. 
Note: In the event of a CIP Exceptional Circumstance where processes in this procedure cannot be 
followed, follow the processes detailed in the LSPG OT CIP Exceptional Circumstances procedure 
to request and document a CIP Exceptional Circumstance to maintain compliance with NERC CIP 
Standards. 
3.1.1 
An LSPG employee creates an AR in the Change Management Solution.  
3.1.2 
The initiator selects what access is required and submits the request. For details on 
completing the AR please refer to LSPG Service Request Work Instruction.  
3.1.3 
OT Security & Compliance receives a task to validate PRA & CIP training dates. Once validated 
the request moves into the approval stage. 
3.1.4 
The request goes to the employee’s or contractor’s direct manager for their review and 
approval.  
• 
The direct manager reviews the form for accuracy and determines that the access is 
needed for the employee or contractor based on their job responsibilities.  
3.1.5 
After the Direct Manager approves the request goes to OT Security Management for final 
review and approval. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 17 
 
• 
If the request is filled out correctly and there is a business need for the requestee to 
have access, OT Security Management approves the request. 
• 
If the request is missing information or there appears to be no need for access, OT 
Security Management contacts the direct manager to discuss and does not approve the 
request until the issue is resolved. 
Note: When an AR is approved for employees or contractors for unescorted physical access, 
electronic access, or access to BCSI, the AR will create tasks to complete. These tasks detail steps 
taken to grant access including review of provisioned access.

units.requirement_text: Verify at least once each calendar quarter that individuals with active electronic access or unescorted physical access have authorization records.
units.section_text:
3.1 
Quarterly and 15-month Review Overview 
3.1.1 
LSPG shall conduct reviews of individuals with active electronic access, unescorted 
physical access, and associated authorization records, including BCSI access, on a 
quarterly basis and at least once every 15 calendar months. 
3.1.2 
Quarterly and 15-calendar-month reviews require managers to validate that access 
privileges and authorizations remain appropriate for each of their direct reports. 
3.1.3 
OT Compliance will initiate and assign access reviews via email and track through the 
Change Management Solution. Reviewers will be provided access information only for 
personnel within their direct reporting structure. 
3.1.4 
The Compliance Tracking Tool automatically generates a task to complete the access 
review every 3-months and 15 calendar months.   
3.1.5 
After the evidence of the review has been uploaded to the Compliance Tracking Tool task, 
it is sent to the Manager, OT Security & Compliance for review and approval. 
Steps to Take  
3.2 
Electronic and Physical Access Review of Accounts, Privileges, and BCSI 
3.2.1 
This is the same process for both quarterly and 15-month reviews 
3.2.2 
The scope of this review is to verify that all individuals with provisioned access to the BES, 
associated EACMS, PACS and BCSI have an authorization record and still have a business 
need for access.  This includes employees, contractors, and vendors with access. 
3.2.2.1 
Scope includes but is not limited to:  
• 
High Impact BES Cyber Systems and their associated: 1. EACMS; and 2. PACS  
• 
Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems with External Routable Connectivity and 
their associated: 1. EACMS; and 2. PACS 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 6 of 8 
 
Steps to Take (to be performed for both electronic access and unescorted physical 
access authorizations): 
1) 
Review the standard to validate requirement and current version is correct. 
2) Create a staging folder for all evidence (folder label should include quarter/year 
identifier): L:\T_CTT\81.0 OT\CIP-004\Quarterly Access Reviews 
3) Compile system generated list of the following: 
1. 
Authorization records from change management solution 
2. Active users, accounts, and associated security groups including. 
• 
list of active personnel and vendors (domain and local accounts) 
• 
list of domain accounts (shared accounts) 
• 
list of local accounts (shared accounts) 
• 
list of active physical access accounts (PACS report) 
• 
PMP report (request from OT Compliance) 
3. BCSI repositories 
a. Request the following from OT security Operations. 
• 
S:\ Drive Operations Access Report  
• 
S:\ Drive Sysadmin Access Report 
• 
S:\ Drive Field Ops Access Report  
• 
OneDrive Access Report 
• 
ShareFile Access 
• 
Adept 
• 
Laserfiche Access Report 
• 
Armortext User Report 
• 
BigFix User Report 
• 
SFTP User Report 
b. Request the following from Field Operations: 
• 
PowerBase User Report 
c. Request the following from IT department: 
• 
T_CTT Folder Access Report 
d. Request the following from Transmission Compliance: 
• 
AssurX Access 
4. Verify all active users have authorization records and that that access was 
authorized prior to being granted. 
5. Map CIP users to managers as recorded in the Configuration Management 
Database (CMDB). 
6. Create user access sheets for each direct manager in CMDB. 
7. Email list of users, privileges, and current provisioning to direct managers for 
review and approval.  BCC changegear@lspower.com so the communication 
creates a ticket in the ticket management solution for tracking. 
8. After manager reviews are complete, stage all evidence for review.   
9. Create a summary report of findings and compile all lists into a master 
workbook. 
10. Open peer review ticket and assign it to OT Security and Compliance analyst. 
11. Once peer review is complete, attach completed workbook, source 
documents, and manager approvals/communication of validating existing 
privileges. 
12. Request approval. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 8 
 
 Evidence to be collected: 
• 
Manager Access Review Sheets 
• 
Direct Manager Approvals of Access 
• 
Source Access Reports 
• 
Peer Review

3.1.3 
OT Compliance will initiate and assign access reviews via email and track through the 
Change Management Solution. Reviewers will be provided access information only for 
personnel within their direct reporting structure. 
3.1.4

review every 3-months and 15 calendar months.   
3.1.5 
After the evidence of the review has been uploaded to the Compliance Tracking Tool task, 
it is sent to the Manager, OT Security & Compliance for review and approval.

3.2

associated EACMS, PACS and BCSI have an authorization record and still have a business 
need for access.  This includes employees, contractors, and vendors with access.

•

3.1.5 
Access Revocation Program (R5) 
3.1.5.1 
LSPG shall document and implement an access revocation program to remove an individual’s 
access to BES Cyber Systems based upon the following conditions and timeframes: 
• 
For any termination action:  
o 
Revoke ability for unescorted physical access and Interactive Remote Access and 
complete the removals within 24 hours (Part 5.1);  
o 
Remove the individual’s ability to use provisioned access to BCSI by the end of the 
next calendar day following the effective date of the termination action (Part 6.3);  
o 
Revoke access to non-shared accounts within 30 days of the effective date of the 
termination action (Part 5.3, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and associated 
EACMS only); and/or 
o 
Change passwords to shared accounts known to the user within 30 calendar days 
of the termination action (Part 5.4, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and 
associated EACMS only)  
 
If LSPG determines there are extenuating operating circumstances which 
require a longer period of time for the password not to be changed, LSPG shall 
document such circumstances and change the shared account password 
within 10 calendar days following the end of the operating circumstance (Part 
5.4).

3.3 Disable or Termination of Accounts

Procedure within 24 hours of the termination action.

conditions and duration of the leave. If OT Security Management determines the access 
should be disabled, the access shall remain disabled until the user’s Supervisor/Manager 
requests re-activation. 
3.3.3 If an individual is reassigned or transferred (job responsibility change), the user’s access is 
revoked per OT Access Management Procedure within 24 hours of the date it is determined 
the user no longer requires access.

and/or monitoring of LSPG ESPs. 
1.3.4

LSPG Physical Security Perimeters (PSPs). 
1.3.5 
Protected Cyber Assets (PCAs) within ESPs.

units.requirement_text: Require multi-factor authentication for all Interactive Remote Access sessions.
units.section_text:
3.2.2 Access Methods 
3.2.2.1 
LSPG shall, where technically feasible, utilizes an Intermediate System such that the 
system outside an ESP may not initiate Interactive Remote Access (IRA) with a CIP Cyber 
Asset inside an ESP.  
3.2.2.2 
Intermediate Systems are maintained and monitored by OT Security Operations. 
3.2.2.3 
Restrictive firewall rules will be used and only ports and protocols required for accessing 
the Intermediate System servers will be allowed. 
3.2.2.4 
Where technically feasible, encryption shall be utilized between end user devices and 
Intermediate System servers, at a minimum, to protect against unauthorized interception 
of transmissions on communications links. 
3.2.2.5 
Remote access sessions are required to use an RDP client that utilizes encrypted 
communication channels. 
3.2.2.6 
IP ranges used by CIP Cyber Assets to communicate will be limited to known ranges of 
LSPG IP addresses on specific subnets or individual hosts. 
3.2.2.7 
Internal access to Intermediate Systems is limited to authorized users using specific 
LSPG IP ranges. 
3.2.2.8 
Where technically feasible, multi-factor authentication (MFA) will be used for all 
interactive Intermediate System server sessions, and privileges will be restricted to only 
what is required for authorized users. 
3.2.2.9 
External access to Intermediate Systems is limited to authorized users using only OT 
approved and maintained Multi-Factor Authentication methods, from specific LSPG IP 
ranges.

units.requirement_text: Restrict physical access to cabling and other nonprogrammable communication components used for connection between applicable Cyber Assets within the same Electronic Security Perimeter in those instances when such cabling and components are located outside of a Physical Security Perimeter. Where physical access restrictions to such cabling and components are not implemented, the Responsible Entity shall document and implement one or more of the following: - encryption of data that transits such cabling and components; or - monitoring the status of the communication link composed of such cabling and components and issuing an alarm or alert in response to detected communication failures to the personnel identified in the BES Cyber Security Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection; or - an equally effective logical protection.

Define operational or procedural controls to restrict physical access (Part 1.1), 
• 
Utilize at least one physical access control to allow unescorted physical access into

• 
Where technically feasible, utilize two or more different physical access controls (this 
does not require two completely independent physical access control systems) to

3.2 Physical Security Perimeters (PSP) 
3.2.1 
LSPG has established PSPs to protect High Impact and Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems. 
3.2.2 Access Control Points (ACP) into PSPs have, at a minimum, the controls defined below to 
ensure physical security: 
3.2.2.1 
Position sensors/switches are required for all ACPs. If the ACP is a double door, each 
door shall require a door position switch. 
3.2.2.2 
Fail-secure electrified locking hardware. 
3.2.2.3 
All ACPs are configured to alert in case of an unauthorized access attempt. Refer to 
Section 3.7 for more information on logging, monitoring, and alerting of physical access.

3.7.8 Visually Detected Unauthorized Access 
3.7.8.1 
Notification to the Transmission Operations Manager (or designee) is required after 
detection of unauthorized access through a physical access point into a PSP or 
unauthorized physical access to a PACS within 15 minutes of the detection. Alerts include 
but are not limited to: 
• 
Detected physical damage to an ACP or local controller (e.g., controls 
partially/completely disabled) 
• 
Detected physical breach of an ACP 
• 
Detected electronic breach of an ACP

3.5.2 The primary ACM is located within a PSP at the TX Primary Control Center. The redundant 
ACM is located within the PSP at the TX Backup Control Center. 
3.5.3 The local controller inherits all the security measures implemented to protect the PSP. Each 
cabinet has a tamper switch as an additional physical security control. Each tamper switch 
has been configured to notify the Transmission System Operator (TSO) of any unauthorized 
access. 
3.5.4 The PACS is configured to monitor and log access 24x7 to the PSPs through its access 
control devices (e.g., card readers, PIN pads, door sensors, and local controllers). 
3.5.5 The PACS creates a log entry for, at a minimum: 
3.5.5.1 
Valid access card read 
3.5.5.2 Invalid access card read 
3.5.5.3 Door held open past threshold – 30 seconds 
3.5.5.4 Door forced 
3.5.5.5 Deactivated card attempt 
3.5.5.6 Tamper Notification 
3.5.6 In the event of PACS unavailability, loss of integrity of a PSP border, or other similar impacts 
on the physical security of a PSP, alternative measures shall be implemented for the duration 
of the event. These measures may include: 
3.5.6.1 
The use of physical keys to enter and/or exit a PSP in the event of a component or system 
failure. Refer to OT Key Management Work Instruction for guidance on obtaining a 
physical key. 
3.5.6.2 Video Surveillance – may only be used for investigative purposes only. 
3.5.6.3 Deploying an LSPG employee or contractor with authorized unescorted physical access 
to the PSP (within 15 minutes of notification of a system failure) to monitor the ACP until 
the PACS is restored. Logging of personnel into and out of the PSP during this time will 
be manually documented

3.3.1 
Physical Security Plan (R1) 
3.3.1.1 
LSPG shall document and implement one or more physical security plans that: 
• 
Define operational or procedural controls to restrict physical access (Part 1.1), 
• 
Utilize at least one physical access control to allow unescorted physical access into 
each applicable Physical Security Perimeter to only those individuals who have 
authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.2), 
• 
Where technically feasible, utilize two or more different physical access controls (this 
does not require two completely independent physical access control systems) to 
collectively allow unescorted physical access into Physical Security Perimeters to only 
those individuals who have authorized unescorted physical access (Part 1.3, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS and PCA only), 
• 
Monitor for unauthorized access through a physical access point into a Physical Security 
Perimeter (Part 1.4), 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 10 of 28 
 
• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized access through a physical 
access point into a Physical Security Perimeter to the personnel identified in the Cyber 
Security Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection (Part 1.5), 
• 
Monitor each Physical Access Control System for unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System (Part 1.6), 
• 
Issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized physical access to a 
Physical Access Control System to the personnel identified in the Cyber Security 
Incident response plan within 15 minutes of the detection (Part 1.7), 
• 
Log (through automated means or by personnel who control entry) entry of each 
individual with authorized unescorted physical access into each Physical Security 
Perimeter, with information to identify the individual and date and time of entry (Part 
1.8), 
• 
Retain physical access logs of entry of individuals with authorized unescorted physical 
access into each Physical Security Perimeter for at least 90 calendar days (Part 1.9), and 
• 
Restrict physical access to cabling and other nonprogrammable communication 
components used for connection between applicable Cyber Assets within the same 
Electronic Security Perimeter in those instances when such cabling and components are 
located outside of a Physical Security Perimeter (Part 1.10). 
o 
Where physical access restrictions are not implemented, LSPG shall document and 
implement one or more of the following: 
 
Encryption of data that transits such cabling and components; or 
 
Monitoring the status of the communication link composed of such cabling 
and components and issuing an alarm or alert in response to detected 
communication failures to the personnel identified in the BES Cyber Security 
Incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection; or 
 
An equally effective logical protection.

units.section_text:
3.9 Declaring and responding to CIP Exceptional Circumstances 
Note: The processes for declaring a CIP Exceptional Circumstance covers high impact and 
medium impact BCS, and assets containing low impact BCS. 
3.9.1 
The CIP Senior Manager, or approved delegate, may declare an emergency as allowed per the 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Procedure and may suspend any or all the following cyber 
security requirements: 
3.9.1.1 
Requirement to complete security training prior to authorization for unescorted physical 
access and/or authorization for electronic access to BES Cyber Systems (CIP-004 R2.2), 
3.9.1.2 
Requirement to authorize electronic or physical access based on need (CIP-004 R4.1), 
3.9.1.3 
Requirement for continuous visitor escort while within a Physical Security Perimeter (CIP-
006 R2.1), 
3.9.1.4 
Requirement for manual or automatic logging of visitor access to a Physical Security 
Perimeter (CIP-006 R2.2), 
3.9.1.5 
Requirement to retain applicable (security monitoring) event logs for at least the last 90 
consecutive calendar days (CIP-007 R4.3), and 
3.9.1.6 
Allow for Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media that include the sections in 
Attachment 1 (CIP-010 R4, CIP-003 Att. 1 Sections 5.1 and 5.2). 
LSPG shall document the suspension of any of these cyber security policies including the reason and 
duration. Delegates are documented in a separate document maintained by the Reliability Compliance 
department.

3.7 Logical Ports and Services 
3.7.1 
A ports and services baseline consists of the following information/ documentation for each 
active/listening service, protocol and port/port range within a CIP Cyber Asset. 
3.7.1.1 
Name of the service executable. 
3.7.1.2 
Ports and/or port ranges usable by the service 
3.7.1.3 
Protocol(s) usable by the service 
3.7.1.4 
Service, port and protocol justification  
3.7.2 For applicable CIP Cyber Assets, at a minimum, logical ports and services that are not 
required for normal or emergency operations shall be disabled on devices within the scope 
of this procedure.  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 10 of 22 
 
3.7.2.1 
If the logical ports running on a device cannot be accurately identified to ensure that 
only unnecessary ports or services will be disabled, the device will be considered to 
have no provision for disabling or restricting logical ports and all ports and services on 
the device shall be considered as necessary. 
3.7.3 Ports and services are considered to be required if: 
3.7.3.1 
For a service/port/protocol to be considered required, the appropriate justification 
must be established and documented. 
3.7.3.2 
Adequate justification for services consists of two components: 
• 
Purpose – A description of what the service is used for; 
• 
Necessity – Adequate justification for a port/port range/protocol consists of 
approved vendor documentation or attestation (see Appendix 2) by an SME that 
the port/port range/protocol is used by a required service and that the port/port 
range/protocol is required for the service to operate.  
3.7.3.3 
The service provides the required functionality as designed by the installed application 
and the application will not provide the desired functionality without it. 
3.7.3.4 
The ports used by the service are required for the service to function or if it is by design 
that the port cannot be disabled. 
3.7.3.5 
Any port and/or service identified or is utilized for emergency operations within the 
RFC.

units.requirement_text:
[CIP-007-6 R2 Part 2.1] A patch management process for tracking, evaluating, and installing cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. The tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that the Responsible Entity tracks for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are updateable and for which a patching source exists.
[CIP-007-6 R2 Part 2.2] At least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources identified in Part 2.1.
[CIP-007-6 R2 Part 2.3] For applicable patches identified in Part 2.2, within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion, take one of the following actions: - Apply the applicable patches; or - Create a dated mitigation plan; or - Revise an existing mitigation plan. Mitigation plans shall include the Responsible Entity’s planned actions to mitigate the vulnerabilities addressed by each security patch and a timeframe to complete these mitigations.
[CIP-007-6 R2 Part 2.4] For each mitigation plan created or revised in Part 2.3, implement the plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the timeframe specified in Part 2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate.
units.section_text:
3.4.2 Security Patch Management Process (R2) 
3.4.2.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a patch management process to: 
• 
Track, evaluate, and install cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. The 
tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that LSPG tracks 
for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are 
updateable and for which a patching source exists (Part 2.1), 
• 
At least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that 
have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources (Part 2.2), 
• 
Within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion (of applicable security patches) 
take one of the following actions: 
o 
Apply the applicable security patches, 
o 
Create a dated mitigation plan, and 
o 
Revise an existing mitigation plan. 
• 
Develop mitigation plans and include planned actions to mitigate the vulnerabilities 
addressed by each security patch and a timeframe to complete these mitigations (Part 
2.3), and 
• 
For each mitigation plan created or revised, LSPG shall implement the plan within the 
timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the 
timeframe specified is approved by the CIP Senior Manager (or Designee) (Part 2.4).

The patch shall be deemed to be an applicable security patch if the patch meets ALL of 
the criteria below: 
3.3.3.1 
The patch or update is for a currently installed version of the application. 
3.3.3.2 
Utilizing Foxguard, vendor notifications, if applicable, and SME expertise of the 
application to identify if a patch addresses a security vulnerability. 
3.3.3.3 
SME will also review the current infrastructure and device functionality to 
further determine applicability. 
3.3.4 
All data collected or created during the discovery and initial evaluation process for 
security patches, by Foxguard, shall be entered directly into the applicable patch 
evaluation workbook which may include but is not limited to: 
3.3.4.1 
Download link to the vendor patch source. 
3.3.4.2 
Foxguard patch quantity evidence link. 
3.3.4.3 
Vendor documentation, release notes and/or release notes link for the patch. 
3.3.5 
Upon review and completion of the discovery and initial evaluation performed, the SME 
shall provide their applicable patch evaluation workbook to the OT Security & Compliance 
SME. The patch workbook(s) may include: 
3.3.5.1 
Vendor – the vendor associated with the product, application, OS, or firmware 
3.3.5.2 
Product – the product, application, OS, or firmware for which the patch or 
upgrade applies 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 9 of 14 
 
3.3.5.3 
Version – the version, being tracked, to determine if a newer version is available 
3.3.5.4 
Patch Name – version of the newly released patch, if applicable 
3.3.5.5 
Review Date – date the vendor, Foxguard, reviewed the new patch 
3.3.5.6 
Release Date – date vendor released new patch, if applicable 
3.3.5.7 
Update Type – type of patch released, if applicable 
3.3.5.8 
Download Link – link, to the vendor site, to download the new patch executable 
file 
3.3.5.9 
Patch Quantity Evidence Link – vendor, Foxguard, link to the screenshot 
documenting the patch release date on the vendors website   
3.3.5.10 Release Notes Link – link, to the vendor release notes, on the vendor site, if 
applicable 
3.3.5.11 
Applicable – denotes if the released patch is/is not applicable to LSPG 
3.3.5.12 Installed by (Month Day, Year) – denotes if the released patch will/will not be 
installed by the respective 35th calendar day 
3.3.5.13 Ticket Number [RFC/SR] – indicates the RFC or mitigation plan number 
associated with the patch installation 
3.3.5.14 Patch Evaluation Date – date internal Patch Evaluation meeting occurs 
3.3.6 
Management shall review the applicable patch evaluation workbooks for applicability and 
provide the final decision, for applicability, of any security and potential security patches. 
This final determination completes the discovery and evaluation phase.

units.section_text:
3.6 Patch Mitigation Plan Management  
3.6.1 
Applicable security patches determined not able to be installed within 35 calendar days 
of evaluation are added to a mitigation plan by creating a dated mitigation plan or revising 
an existing mitigation plan within the Change Management Solution. 
3.6.2 
Mitigation plans shall include a list of patches, LSPG’s planned actions, and/or 
implemented mitigating controls to mitigate the vulnerabilities addressed by each 
security patch, and a timeframe to complete any mitigations that are not in effect. 
3.6.3 
LSPG maintains mitigation plans within the Change Management Solution which serve to 
document patches that cannot, or have not, been deployed and the associated mitigating 
measures to reduce risk. 
3.6.4 
SMEs will review their applicable patch mitigation plans during each patch evaluation 
cycle. The mitigation plan review will include determining if the plan is still valid and is on 
schedule to be completed by the assigned mitigation date.  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 11 of 14 
 
3.6.5 
Any mitigation plans that are identified as either no longer needed, require revision of 
mitigation plan actions or the completion date is at risk, will be escalated to OT 
Security/EMS/Field Operations Management. 
3.6.6 
The Creator of the mitigation plan shall update each mitigation plan as directed by 
management by completing one of the following actions 
3.6.6.1 
Acknowledgement that the MP is still valid and required.  
3.6.6.2 
Changes needed. (ex. Version of software change) 
3.6.6.3 
Update timeline for resolution of issue 
3.6.7 
The LSPG CIP Senior Manager, or delegate, will be responsible for approving any new or 
revised mitigation plan.

further directions.

units.section_text:
3.4.2 Security Patch Management Process (R2) 
3.4.2.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a patch management process to: 
• 
Track, evaluate, and install cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets. The 
tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that LSPG tracks 
for the release of cyber security patches for applicable Cyber Assets that are 
updateable and for which a patching source exists (Part 2.1), 
• 
At least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that 
have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources (Part 2.2), 
• 
Within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion (of applicable security patches) 
take one of the following actions: 
o 
Apply the applicable security patches, 
o 
Create a dated mitigation plan, and 
o 
Revise an existing mitigation plan. 
• 
Develop mitigation plans and include planned actions to mitigate the vulnerabilities 
addressed by each security patch and a timeframe to complete these mitigations (Part 
2.3), and 
• 
For each mitigation plan created or revised, LSPG shall implement the plan within the 
timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the 
timeframe specified is approved by the CIP Senior Manager (or Designee) (Part 2.4).

units.requirement_text: Review a summarization or sampling of logged events as determined by the Responsible Entity at intervals no greater than 15 calendar days to identify undetected Cyber Security Incidents.
units.section_text:
3.5 CMLAP Log Review for CIP High Impact BES Cyber Systems, EACM, and PCA Devices 
3.5.1 
For CIP Cyber Assets where logs are maintained by a CMLAP: 
3.5.1.1 
OT shall review a summarization or sampling of logged events for Applicable Systems, at 
a minimum at intervals no greater than fifteen (15) calendar days, to identify undetected 
Cyber Security Incidents. 
• 
Completion of this review shall be documented in a Compliance Tracking Tool task. 
• 
OT will escalate all potential cybersecurity incidents to OT Security Management. 
3.5.2 For CIP Cyber Assets, where logs are not maintained by a CMLAP with automated alerting 
capability, OT shall review these logs, as close to daily as possible, to detect any real or 
suspected Cyber Security Incidents. 
3.5.2.1 
Log review shall be documented and performed, as described in  Appendix 2: Steps for 
Manual Log Review 
3.5.3 All Cyber Security Incidents that are identified by a log review shall trigger execution of OT 
Security Incident Response Procedure by either the OT Security Operations or OT Security & 
Compliance team upon notification or the reviewing entity. 
3.5.4 Upon discovery of a real or suspected reportable Cyber Security Incident, involving CIP Cyber 
Assets, all related logs and information shall be collected, retained, and be provided upon 
request, as documented in OT Security Incident Response Procedure.

units.section_text:
3.4.5 System Access Controls Process (R5) 
3.4.5.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a system access control process to: 
• 
Define a method(s) to enforce authentication of interactive user access, where 
technically feasible (Part 5.1), 
• 
Identify and inventory all known enabled default or other generic account types, either 
by system, by groups of systems, by location, or by system type(s) (Part 5.2), 
• 
Identify individuals who have authorized access to shared accounts (Part 5.3), 
• 
Change known default passwords, per Cyber Asset capability (Part 5.4), and 
• 
For password-only authentication for interactive user access, either technically or 
procedurally, enforce the following password parameters (Part 5.5): 
o 
Password length that is, at least, the lesser of eight characters or the maximum 
length supported by the Cyber Asset (Part 5.5.1), and 
o 
Minimum password complexity that is the lesser of three or more different types 
of characters (e.g., uppercase alphabetic, lowercase alphabetic, numeric, non- 
alphanumeric) or the maximum complexity supported by the Cyber Asset (Part 
5.5.2). 
• 
For password-only authentication for interactive user access, where technically 
feasible, either technically or procedurally enforce password changes or an obligation 
to change the password at least once every 15 calendar months (Part 5.6), and 
• 
LSPG shall, where technically feasible, either: 
o 
Limit the number of unsuccessful authentication attempts, or 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 13 of 28 
 
o 
Generate alerts after a threshold of unsuccessful authentication attempts (Part 
5.7).

5.5 Classify Cyber Security Incidents as Reportable or Attempt to Compromise 
The SIRT will review available data and attempt to identify and classify the cyber security incident 
using Table 5.1 Classify Cyber Security Incidents.  
The SIRT has discretion to assign an Incident Severity Level and whether to report to E‐ISAC, NCCIC, 
ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, CAISO or other agencies based upon the symptoms and circumstance. The SIRT 
has one or more processes to determine if an identified Cyber Security Incident is a Reportable Cyber 
Security Incident or an attempt to compromise and to notify the E‐ISAC, NCCIC, ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 16 of 46 
 
CAISO and other agencies, unless prohibited by law. Initial notification to the E‐ISAC, NCCIC, ERCOT, 
PJM, NYISO, CAISO and other agencies which may be only a preliminary notice, shall not exceed one hour 
from the determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident.

units.section_text:
1.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this work instruction is to outline the processes that OT Security Operations / OT 
Security & Compliance should adhere to when responding to cyber security incidents related to 
malicious code. The purpose of the process is to facilitate a timely, coordinated, and repeatable 
response process across the department to: 
• 
Conduct a detailed and timely assessment and triage of potential incidents. 
• 
Minimize the business impact of a cyber security incident. 
• 
Provide a streamlined approach to managing a cyber security incident. 
• 
Define and assign the roles and responsibilities that are required to deliver an effective 
response.

units.section_text:
5.0 Incident Handling Procedure 
The NIST Cyber Security Framework forms the core functions of the CSIRP used to manage risk and 
the impact from Cyber Security Events to BES Cyber Systems/Assets, See Figure 3‐1 LSPG CISRP 
Functions, based on NIST Cyber Security Framework, Version 1.1, dated 4/16/2018. The framework and 
supporting activities are not intended to form a serial path or lead to a static desired end state; the 
following activities can be performed concurrently and continuously to form an operational culture 
that addresses the dynamics of cyber security risk.

units.requirement_text: Incident handling procedures for Cyber Security Incidents.
units.section_text:
1.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this work instruction is to outline the processes that OT Security Operations / OT 
Security & Compliance should adhere to when responding to cyber security incidents related to 
malicious code. The purpose of the process is to facilitate a timely, coordinated, and repeatable 
response process across the department to: 
• 
Conduct a detailed and timely assessment and triage of potential incidents. 
• 
Minimize the business impact of a cyber security incident. 
• 
Provide a streamlined approach to managing a cyber security incident. 
• 
Define and assign the roles and responsibilities that are required to deliver an effective 
response.

units.section_text:
7.3 Security Incident Response Plan Updates 
7.3.1 
No later than ninety (90) calendar days after the completion of a test or actual response to a 
Reportable Cyber Security Incident response:  
7.3.1.1 
Any lessons learned or the absence of any lessons learned shall be documented on the 
Security Incident Investigation Form. 
7.3.1.2 
This Plan shall be updated based on any documented lessons learned associated with 
the plan.  
7.3.1.3 
Each person or group with a defined role in this Plan shall be notified of the updates 
made as a result of testing the plan or an actual Reportable Cyber Security Incident. 
7.3.1.4 
Specific after-action items, not including procedure updates, should be identified and 
tracked in Compliance Tracking Tool to closure. 
7.3.2 No later than sixty (60) calendar days after a change to the roles or responsibilities or a 
change in technology that would impact the ability to execute this procedure:  
7.3.2.1 
This Plan shall be updated to reflect the change(s).  
7.3.2.2 
Notification shall be sent to each person or group with a defined role in Section 3.2 that 
the evidence is located in the LSPG Compliance Tracking tool. 
7.3.3 Records generated from a Reportable Cyber Security incident shall be maintained for a 
minimum of three (3) years, or longer if directed by the Reliability Compliance Team to retain 
longer due to an investigation.

3.5.4.1 
For high, medium, and low impact BCS, and their associated EACMS, LSPG shall communicate 
Reportable Cyber Security Incidents to E-ISAC or if subject to the jurisdiction of the United 
States, the United States National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center: 
• 
Initial notifications and updates shall include the following attributes, at a minimum, to 
the extent known: (Part 4.1) 
o 
The functional impact (Part 4.1.1);  
o 
The attack vector used (Part 4.1.2); and  
o 
The level of intrusion that was achieved or attempted (Part 4.1.3).  
• 
After the Responsible Entity’s determination made pursuant to documented 
process(es) in Requirement R1, Part 1.2, provide initial notification within the following 
timelines (Part 4.2): 
o 
One hour after the determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident. 
o 
By the end of the next calendar day after determination that a Cyber Security 
Incident was an attempt to compromise a system identified in the “Applicable 
Systems” column for this Part.

6.1.7 
Reporting Timeframes (Applicable to CIP) 
6.1.7.1 
If the incident was determined to be a Reportable Cyber Security Incident by the SIRT 
Team and the Director, Operations Technology, the SIRT Lead has one (1) hour to 
complete the OE-417 form Reliability First and/or other methods to notify E-ISAC and 
NCCIC.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date and time when the determination was made, and 
date and time the form was submitted are captured on the Security Incident 
Investigation Form. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 23 of 46 
 
6.1.7.2 
If the incident was determined to be an attempt to compromise a system, the SIRT Lead 
has until the end of the next calendar day to complete and submits the appropriate 
form(s) to E-ISAC and NCCIC.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date and time when the determination was made, and 
date and time the form was submitted are captured on the Security Incident 
Investigation Form. 
6.1.7.3 
The SIRT Lead provides updates to E-ISAC and NCCIC within 7 calendar days of 
determination of any new or changed information from the initial notification.  
• 
The name of individual(s), date, time, and when the updates were made are 
documented on the Security Incident Investigation Form.

5.5 Classify Cyber Security Incidents as Reportable or Attempt to Compromise 
The SIRT will review available data and attempt to identify and classify the cyber security incident 
using Table 5.1 Classify Cyber Security Incidents.  
The SIRT has discretion to assign an Incident Severity Level and whether to report to E‐ISAC, NCCIC, 
ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, CAISO or other agencies based upon the symptoms and circumstance. The SIRT 
has one or more processes to determine if an identified Cyber Security Incident is a Reportable Cyber 
Security Incident or an attempt to compromise and to notify the E‐ISAC, NCCIC, ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 16 of 46 
 
CAISO and other agencies, unless prohibited by law. Initial notification to the E‐ISAC, NCCIC, ERCOT, 
PJM, NYISO, CAISO and other agencies which may be only a preliminary notice, shall not exceed one hour 
from the determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident.

3.1 Recovery Plan 
3.1.1 
LSPG has developed and implemented a series of processes, procedures and work 
instructions to restore in-scope systems from unpredicted cyber or physical event(s) that 
impact the reliability and operation of all OT managed systems. The Recovery Plan describes 
the process to assess the conditions for the activation of the Recovery Plan, the roles and 
responsibilities of responders, and the backup and storage process to recover BES Cyber 
System functionality.

units.section_text:
7.2 Lessons Learned Documentation 
7.2.1 
No later than ninety (90) calendar days after the completion of a test or a response to an 
actual Reportable Security Incident response, any lessons learned associated with the plan 
shall be documented as high medium, and low OR the absence of any lessons learned shall 
be documented. 
7.2.2 The SIRT shall be allowed to provide comments and suggested lessons learned for at least 
five (5) business days after the event has concluded. 
7.2.2.1 
Lessons Learned associated with the plan are documented on the Security Incident 
Investigation Form. Process improvements that are not related to the plan are 
documented separately and provided to department managers. 
7.2.3 A meeting(s) shall be held with all members of the OT Security Operations and/or OT Security 
& Compliance and other identified key stakeholders, as determined by event details, to 
discuss the lessons learned. During this meeting(s), the following items shall be completed: 
7.2.3.1 
Lessons learned will be assigned owners and/or owner groups. 
• 
Not every lesson learned item will be assigned an OT owner. OT will only take 
responsibility for OT related actions. 
• 
Some lessons learned may be identified as not actionable and will not be assigned 
an owner. 
7.2.3.2 
Assigned action owners will be asked to provide recommended due dates for the action. 
7.2.4 The composed lessons learned list shall be reviewed and approved by the SIRT Core Team. 
7.2.5 The composed lessons learned shall be scanned, saved, and uploaded to the LSPG 
Compliance Tracking Tool. 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 25 of 46 
 
7.2.6 The SIRT Core Team member will notify each person or group with a defined roles in Section 
3.2 that the document has been scanned, saved and uploaded to the LSPG Compliance 
Tracking tool.

3.7.1 
Configuration Change Management Process (R1) 
3.7.1.1 
LSPG shall develop, document, and implement a configuration change management process 
to: 
• 
Establish a baseline configuration, individually or by group, which shall include the 
following elements (Part 1.1): 
o 
Operating system(s) (including version) or firmware where no independent 
operating system exists (Part 1.1.1), 
o 
Any commercially available or open-source application software (including 
version) intentionally installed (Part 1.1.2), 
o 
Any custom software installed (Part 1.1.3), 
o 
Any logical network accessible ports (Part 1.1.4), and 
o 
Any security patches applied (Part 1.1.5). 
• 
Authorize and document any changes that deviate from the existing baseline 
configuration (Part 1.2), 
• 
For a change that deviates from the existing baseline configuration (Part 1.3), (Part 1.4), 
(Part 1.5, for High impact BES Cyber Systems only): 
o 
Update the baseline configuration within 30 calendar days of completing the 
change (Part 1.3), 
o 
Prior to the change, determine required cyber security controls in CIP-005 and 
CIP-007 that could be impacted by the change (Part 1.4.1); following the change, 
verify the required cyber security controls are not adversely affected (Part 1.4.2) 
and document the results of the verification (Part 1.4.3), 
o 
Where technically feasible, prior to implementing any change in the production 
environment, test the change in a test environment or test the changes in a 
production environment where the test is performed in a manner that minimizes 
adverse effects, and that models the baseline configuration, to ensure that 
required cyber security controls in CIP-005 and CIP-007 are not adversely 
affected (Part 1.5.1, for High impact BES Cyber Systems only),  
o 
Document the results of the testing and, if a test environment was used, the 
differences between the test environment and the production environment, 
including a description of the measures used to account for any differences in 
operation between the test and production environments (Part 1.5.2, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems only), and 
o 
Prior to a change that deviates from the existing baseline configuration associated 
with baseline items in Parts 1.1.1, 1.1.2, and 1.1.5, and when the method to do so is 
available to the Responsible Entity from the software source (Part 1.6):  
 
Verify the identity of the software source (Part 1.6.1); and  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 17 of 28 
 
 
Verify the integrity of the software obtained from the software source (Part 
1.6.2).

The VAT Scanner Ports and Services scan is set up to be recurring per 3.1.3, on the in-scope

3.1.3

3.1.5 
Once the VAT Scanner Ports and Services scan has completed and results show in activity

import to Change Monitoring Solution. 
3.1.6 
If network devices or appliances (agentless) are added to the VAT Scanner between the 
weekly automated process, end users should go into the Change Monitoring Solution 
console to the “Tasks” tab, expand the Root Task Group folder, then select Tripwire State

3.1.10

This process also updates the ports and services component of the baseline for the asset. 
3.2 
Configuration Change Monitoring At Least Once Every 35 Days CIP-010-4 R2.1 
3.2.1 
OT Security Operations / OT Security & Compliance team or delegate will perform a periodic 
review, as close to daily as possible, of the OT Last Time Checked Status Report that details 
the communication status of assets reporting to Change Monitoring Solution. 
3.2.2 
A Change Management Solution ticket will be created system with the short description 
“Remediation of OT Last Time Checked Status Report.”

3.2.3 
Once created, confirm that Assigned Tech is the primary SME. 
3.2.4 
Any new nodes on the report will be triaged to confirm they are not related to work being 
performed under an active RFC or incident ticket. 
3.2.4.1 
TCAs are excluded from the scope of this task. 
3.2.5 
The team will investigate nodes to determine if the event is a one-time anomaly or requires 
further investigation. Best efforts will be made to perform the investigation on the same day 
and not to exceed five business days. 
3.2.6 
In-scope CIP Cyber Assets should be prioritized for remediation. 
3.2.7 
Classifications can be validated by going to Asset View, search by host name or IP address, 
and reviewing node Tag Sets as shown in the screenshot below:

3.2.8 
If the Classification is not defined in Change Monitoring Solution, go to OTAM CMDB to 
retrieve the Classification. (Note – If device is not in OTAM CMDB, investigation needs to 
occur via creation of a Change Management Solution ticket) 
• 
Classifications can be updated by: 
• 
Select the check mark before the host name, 
• 
Click Edit Tags in the right menu bar, 
• 
Click the Classification menu and select correct option, 
• 
Click close.

3.2.9 
If event is determined to not be an anomaly and requires further troubleshooting, OT Security 
Operations / OT Security & Compliance team will remediate. 
3.2.10 Remediation includes: 
3.2.10.1 
Document the open RFC impacting connectivity (if applicable). 
3.2.10.2 Log into the asset and restart the Change Monitoring Solution agent (servers and 
workstations). 
3.2.10.3 Reinstall Configuration Change Monitoring Solution agent. 
3.2.10.4 For agentless assets (network devices/appliances), contact the assigned SME about 
configuration change that is impacting communication with Change Monitoring Solution 
console. 
3.2.11 
If the assigned SME is not available, forward the ticket to the SME on call. 
3.2.12 
Once the assigned SME performs remediation, the ticket should be routed back to the 
Primary SME for validation that asset is reporting back to Change Monitoring Solution. 
Once configuration change monitoring is validated as reporting to the solution, the Primary 
SME should document resolution notes in the ticket and close it. 
3.3 
Develop, Authorizing and Document Changes That Deviate from Existing Baseline 
Configuration CIP-010-4 R1.1, R1.2 and R1.3 
3.3.1 
Change promotions in Change Monitoring Solution require research and validation against 
the changes described in the official RFC. 
3.3.2 
Change Monitoring Solution detects deviations from the baseline. OT Security Operations/ 
OT Security & Compliance is required to validate that changes are authorized before 
promoting (approving) the new baseline.  
Separation of duties 
a. Detection of unauthorized changes alert configured (Daily Tripwire Report is 
generated). 
i. 
OT Security and Compliance SMEs investigate. 
ii. 
Any software that is not authorized through RFC or other ticketing processes 
needs to be escalated for review.

b. Detection of unauthorized changes / Promotion to baseline 
i. 
OT Security and Compliance SMEs investigate. 
ii. 
Any software that is not authorized through RFC or other ticketing processes 
needs to be escalated for review. 
iii. 
Software changes should not be promoted to baseline without authorization. 
3.3.2.1 
Authorized changes: an RFC includes the hostname and/or IP address and is within the 
documented timeframe of when the change took place. For example, when security 
patches are applied, all changes to the host will be timestamped and match the 
expected results related to operating system or firmware updates. 
3.3.2.2 
Unauthorized changes: changes to the company’s assets with no RFC. This indicates 
employees/contractors are not following the formal change management process OR is 
an indicator of compromise on the company’s network. 
3.3.3 
Promotion in Change Monitoring Solution creates authorization of the new baseline as 
indicated in the most recent change version. 
3.3.4 
Users can promote element versions for a variety of reasons; for example, if you approve of 
the changes reflected in the latest change version of a file, you can promote the change 
version to the baseline.

implementing the change to the remaining systems.

documented, including a description of the measures used to account for any differences in 
operations between the test and production environments.

production environment in a manner to minimize adverse effects on production systems, 
escalate the RFC to OT Security Operations Management for technical feasibility review.

units.section_text:
3.1 Verify Identity of Software Source and Integrity of Software 
3.1.1 
Prior to a change that deviates from the existing baseline configuration associated with 
applicable baseline items established in CIP-010 R1, Part 1.1, and when a method do so is 
available to LSPG from the software source, LSPG will verify the identity of the software 
source, and verify the integrity of the software obtained from the software source.  
3.1.2 
The applicable items from the baseline established in CIP-010 R1, Part 1.1 are: 
• 
Operating system (OS) or firmware where no independent operating system exists 
(Part 1.1.1) 
• 
Any commercially available or open-source application software (including 
version) intentionally installed (Part 1.1.2) 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 6 of 9 
 
• 
Any security patches applied (Part 1.1.5) 
3.1.3 
The verification methods are based on the source distribution method: 
• 
Automated Source: Software or firmware obtained via an automated process or 
service, such as Security Patch Management software requires documentation of 
the automated source and confirmation of configuration settings in the automated 
service that enforces identity and integrity verification. 
• 
Manual Source: Software, or firmware obtained through manual downloads requires 
documenting the identity of the source (e.g., URL of the download source) and 
integrity verification (e.g., comparison of published MD5 value vs. MD5 value from 
the software package download).  
Note: If no identity or integrity verification method is available, LSPG will document the 
unavailability of a method in the software verification form in the Change Management Solution. 
3.1.4 
SMEs will follow the OT Change Management procedure for all baseline changes. 
3.1.5 
LSPG has created a software verification form within the Change Management Solution to 
document the identity and integrity verification methods used or to document that a method 
for verification does not exist.  
3.1.6 
LSPG may designate a repository to store software package downloads and any relevant 
evidence, including the software verification form.

units.requirement_text: At least once every 15 calendar months, conduct a paper or active vulnerability assessment.
units.section_text:
3.1 Vulnerability Assessments 
3.1.1 
LSPG performs a paper or active VA on High and Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems and 
their associated Electronic Access Control or Monitoring Systems. (EACMS), Protected Cyber 
Assets (PCA), and Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) at least once every 15 calendar 
months. LSPG may conduct a hybrid of active VA for some BES Cyber Systems (BCS), EAMCS, 
PACs and PCAs, and paper VA for the remainder.  
3.1.2 
Where technically feasible, LSPG performs an active VA for BCS identified as High Impact BCS 
at least once every 36 calendar months. This assessment is performed: 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 7 of 15 
 
3.1.2.1 
In a test environment or lab that models the baseline configuration of the BES Cyber 
System/Assets in a production environment 
• 
If an active VA is conducted in a test environment, the OT Security Operations 
Team uses an active monitoring tool to capture the differences between the test 
environment and the production environment, including a description of the 
measures used to account for any differences in operation between the test and 
production environments. This is documented within the associated tasks as part 
of the RFC. 
3.1.2.2 
In a production environment where the test is performed in a manner that minimizes 
adverse effects, actions taken to minimize adverse effects on the production 
environment are documented as part of the RFC. 
3.1.3 
Prior to adding a new, or replacing an existing, applicable BES Cyber Asset, PCA, or EACMS 
associated with a High Impact BES Cyber Systems to a production environment, the OT 
Security & Compliance Team will perform an active VA of the new Cyber Asset. This is 
recorded within the RFC process in Change Management Solution. 
3.1.3.1 
Exceptions include: 
• 
The declaration of CIP Exceptional Circumstances, in accordance with LSPG’s CIP 
Cyber Security Policies. Refer to LSPG CIP-003 Delegate Authority Process. 
• 
If it replaces an applicable Cyber Asset of the same type with a CIP-010-4 R1 
baseline configuration that models an existing baseline configuration of the 
previous or other existing Cyber Asset. In this case, the baseline configuration of 
the new Cyber Asset and the existing baseline configuration will be retained as 
evidence in the associated RFC.  
• 
The OT Security & Compliance Team receives a Compliance Tracking Tool task 
90 days prior to the due date for both the 15 and 36 calendar month vulnerability 
assessments. 
3.1.4 
The OT Security & Compliance Team schedules the days/times for the assessment to be 
performed. 
3.1.4.1 
With approval from the Director, Operations Technology, the OT Security & Compliance 
Team may elect to utilize a third-party vendor to conduct part or all of the vulnerability 
assessment. In this case, the third party is responsible for executing the tasks assigned 
with oversight from the OT Security & Compliance VA Lead. 
3.1.5 
Once the assessment has been completed, the OT Security & Compliance VA Lead compiles 
the documentation of the assessment, attaches it to the Compliance Tracking Tool task, and 
marks it as completed. 
3.2 Paper Vulnerability Assessment –High and Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems, EACMS, 
PACS & PCAs 
3.2.1 
Network Discovery 
3.2.1.1 
The OT Security & Compliance Team, Operations Team, or approved third party vendor, 
performs a review of network connectivity to verify all Electronic Access Points (EAP) 
to the Electronic Security Perimeter (ESP) are documented. This review includes the 
following documents: 

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 8 of 15 
 
• 
List(s) of applicable BES Cyber Systems/Assets and their associated EACMS, PCA, 
and PACS 
• 
List(s) of dial-up devices (or statement that none were found): 
o 
Dial-in or Dial-out 
o 
Hardware (type, firmware, and version) 
• 
EACMS settings/configurations for each in-scope EACMS with an EAP 
• 
ESP network drawing(s) 
3.2.2 Network Ports and Services Identification 
3.2.2.1 
The OT Security & Compliance Team, Operations Team, or approved third party vendor, 
reviews CIP-007-6 R1 documentation to verify that all enabled logical network 
accessible ports and their associated services have an appropriate business 
justification. This includes: 
• 
A review of approved logical network accessible ports and their associated 
services required for the operation of applicable BES Cyber Systems their 
associated EACMS, PCA, and PACS, and 
• 
Verification that business justifications for each port(s) is accurate and sufficient. 
3.2.3 Vulnerability Review 
3.2.3.1 
The OT Security & Compliance Team, Operations Team, or approved third party vendor, 
reviews CIP-005-7 R1 Part 1.3 evidence from each in-scope EAP, as well as CIP-007-6 
R5 Parts 5.2 and 5.4 – 5.6 evidence for default and generic accounts, passwords, and 
network management community strings for each in-scope Cyber Asset. This includes: 
• 
A review of EAP rulesets for inbound and outbound communications to/from each 
ESP to verify that business justifications are accurate, as well as identify overly 
permissive rules, 
• 
A review of default and/or shared operating system, firmware, application, and 
database account inventories to verify accuracy and completeness, 
• 
A review of controls on passwords for those default and/or generic accounts, and 
• 
A review of controls on SNMP community strings. 
3.2.4 Wireless Review 
3.2.4.1 
The OT Security Operations or Field Operations Team identifies common types of 
wireless networks and review their controls if they are in any way used for BES Cyber 
Systems/Assets communication within the ESP. This includes: 
• 
Identification of any wireless networks within the ESP, and 
• 
Verification that wireless controls are in place (i.e., encryption, user access 
control).

3.7.3 Vulnerability Assessments Process (R3) 
3.7.3.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a vulnerability assessment process to: 
• 
At least once every 15 calendar months conduct a paper or active vulnerability 
assessment (Part 3.1), 
• 
Where technically feasible, at least once every 36 calendar months (Part 3.2, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems only): 
o 
Perform an active vulnerability assessment in a test environment, or perform an 
active vulnerability assessment in a production environment where the test is 
performed in a manner that minimizes adverse effects, that models the baseline 
configuration of the BES Cyber System in a production environment (Part 3.2.1, for 
High impact BES Cyber Systems only), and 
o 
Document the results of the testing and, if a test environment was used, the 
differences between the test environment and the production environment, 
including a description of the measures used to account for any differences in 
operation between the test and production environments (Part 3.2.2, for High 
impact BES Cyber Systems only). 
• 
Prior to adding a new applicable Cyber Asset to a production environment, perform an 
active vulnerability assessment of the new Cyber Asset, except for CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances and like replacements of the same type of Cyber Asset with a baseline 
configuration that models an existing baseline configuration of the previous or other 
existing Cyber Asset (Part 3.3, for High impact BES Cyber Systems and associated 
EACMS and PCA). 
• 
LSPG shall document the results of the assessments conducted and the action plan to 
remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities identified in the assessments including the 
planned date of completing the action plan and the execution status of any remediation 
or mitigation action items (Part 3.4).

3.3 NERC CIP Activities Permitted for Delegation 
Pursuant to the NERC CIP Standards certain activities required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager may 
not be delegated. These are activities that the NERC CIP Standards have defined as obligations 
specifically required of the NERC CIP Senior Manager.  
Ownership and accountability for NERC CIP activities that are not CIP Senior Manager obligations are 
managed through other compliance procedures and do not need to be delegated in accordance with 
this Process.  
The following are NERC CIP Standards activities that have been approved by the COO and relevant 
senior leadership for delegation by the CIP Senior Manager:  
CIP Senior Manager Delegations 
3.3.1 
CIP-002-5.1a, R2.2: Approve the identifications of the high, medium, and low BES Cyber 
Systems required by Requirement R1 at least once every 15 calendar months, even if it has no 
identified items in Requirement R1. 
3.3.2 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), R4: The Responsible Entity may delegate authority 
for specific actions under one or more cyber security policies to a delegate or delegates where 
allowed by the NERC CIP Standards. These delegations shall be documented in accordance 
with Section 3.2 and updated within 30 days of any change to the delegation.  
3.3.3 
CIP-007-6, R2.4: For each mitigation plan created or revised in R2.4, Part 2.3, implement the 
plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to 
the timeframe specified in Part 2.3 is approved by the CIP Senior Manager or delegate. 
3.3.4 
CIP-013-2, R3: Each Responsible Entity shall review and obtain CIP Senior Manager or delegate 
approval of its supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) specified in Requirement 
R1 at least once every 15 calendar months. 
CIP Exceptional Circumstance Delegations 
3.3.5 
CIP-003-8 (CIP-003-9, effective 4/1/26), Attachment 1, Section 5: Each Responsible Entity 
shall, except under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, implement plans to achieve the objective 
of mitigating risk of the introduction of malicious code to low impact BES Cyber Systems 
through the use of Transient Cyber Assets and Removable Media. 

[LSP CIP Senior Manager Process] | Page 7 of 10 
Private – For Internal Use Only 
3.3.6 
CIP-004-7, R2.2: Require completion of the training specified in R2.2, Part 2.1 prior to granting 
authorized electronic access and authorized unescorted physical access to applicable Cyber 
Assets, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. 
3.3.7 
CIP-004-7, R4.1-R4.1.3: Process to authorize based on need, as determined by the 
Responsible Entity, except for CIP Exceptional Circumstances: electronic access; unescorted 
physical access into a Physical Security Perimeter; and access to designated storage locations, 
whether physical or electronic, for BES Cyber System Information. 
3.3.8 
CIP-006-6, R2.1 and R2.2: Require continuous escorted access of visitors (individuals who are 
provided access but are not authorized for unescorted physical access) within each Physical 
Security Perimeter, except during CIP Exceptional Circumstances. Require manual or 
automated logging of visitor entry into and exit from the Physical Security Perimeter that 
includes date and time of the initial entry and last exit, the visitor’s name, and the name of an 
individual point of contact responsible for the visitor, except during CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.9 
CIP-007-6, R4.3: Where technically feasible, retain applicable event logs identified in R4.3, Part 
4.1 for at least the last 90 consecutive calendar days except under CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances. 
3.3.10 CIP-010-4, R3.3: Prior to adding a new applicable Cyber Asset to a production environment, 
perform an active vulnerability assessment of the new Cyber Asset, except for CIP Exceptional 
Circumstances and like replacements of the same type of Cyber Asset with a baseline 
configuration that models an existing baseline configuration of the previous or other existing 
Cyber Asset. 
3.3.11 
CIP-010-4, R4: Each Responsible Entity, for its high impact and medium impact BES Cyber 
Systems and associated Protected Cyber Assets, shall implement, except under CIP 
Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) for Transient Cyber Assets and 
Removable Media that include the sections in Attachment 1. 
3.3.12 
CIP-012-1 (CIP-012-2, effective 7/1/26), R1: The Responsible Entity shall implement, except 
under CIP Exceptional Circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) to mitigate the risks 
posed by unauthorized disclosure and unauthorized modification of Real-time Assessment and 
Real-time monitoring data while being transmitted between any applicable Control Centers.

3.2 Protection and Handling Guidelines (Part 1.2) 
All LSPG Personnel, contractors, and vendors, hereinafter referred to as LSPG users, are responsible 
for protecting and maintaining the confidentiality of all BCSI. All LSPG users shall report violations of 
this policy to the Sr. Director, Operations Technology or the Reliability Compliance Team. Any LSPG 
users who violate this program may be subject to adverse action, up to and including termination and 
legal action. If BCSI is found outside a PSP or in a non-CIP protected environment, then LSPG users 
shall shred or destroy the document(s) and notify the Reliability Compliance Team. LSPG users are 
required to delete BCSI data when it is no longer needed.

3.2 Protection and Handling Guidelines (Part 1.2) 
All LSPG Personnel, contractors, and vendors, hereinafter referred to as LSPG users, are responsible 
for protecting and maintaining the confidentiality of all BCSI. All LSPG users shall report violations of 
this policy to the Sr. Director, Operations Technology or the Reliability Compliance Team. Any LSPG 
users who violate this program may be subject to adverse action, up to and including termination and 
legal action. If BCSI is found outside a PSP or in a non-CIP protected environment, then LSPG users 
shall shred or destroy the document(s) and notify the Reliability Compliance Team. LSPG users are 
required to delete BCSI data when it is no longer needed. 
The LSPG Vice President, Reliability Compliance or designee is responsible for the annual review of this 
program.

1.1 
Purpose   
This document addresses NERC CIP-011 that requires a program to identify and provide procedures 
for protecting and securely handling BES Cyber System Information (BCSI) for all BES Cyber Systems 
(BCS) and their associated Electronic Access Control or Monitoring System (EACMS), Physical Access 
Control Systems (PACS), or Protected Cyber Assets (PCAs). This document was developed in 
accordance with CIP Cyber Security Policies.

4.0 Disposal and Reuse Procedures (R2) 
This procedure describes the methods to prevent unauthorized retrieval of BCSI from Cyber Assets 
that are to be disposed of or repurposed.
cited_sentences: This procedure describes the methods to prevent unauthorized retrieval of BCSI from Cyber Assets that are to be disposed of or repurposed.

units.section_text:
3.8.2 BES Cyber Asset Reuse and Disposal Process (R2) 
3.8.2.1 
LSPG shall document and implement a BES Cyber Asset reuse and disposal process to: 
• 
Prior to the release for reuse, prevent the unauthorized retrieval of BCSI from the Cyber 
Asset data storage media prior to the release for reuse of applicable Cyber Assets 
that contain BCSI (except for reuse within like Applicable Systems) (Part 2.1), and 
• 
Prior to the disposal of Cyber Assets, that contain BCSI, prevent the unauthorized 
retrieval of BCSI from the Cyber Asset, or destroy the data storage media (Part 2.2).
